tool_summary: Debian's low-level package tool, the installer apt/apt-get ultimately call. Installs .deb files directly, bypassing repository/signature checks that apt performs, and runs arbitrary maintainer scripts at install/remove time.

rules.description: The --force-* family of flags (--force-all, --force-depends, --force-overwrite, etc.) overrides dpkg's built-in safety checks, allowing installation despite dependency conflicts, file overwrites, or other problems dpkg would otherwise refuse.
rules.reversible_note: The package can be removed, but overwritten files and install-time maintainer script side effects may not be recoverable.

rules.description: Installs a .deb package file directly. This bypasses apt's repository signature verification entirely, since dpkg operates on a local file rather than a trusted repository. Runs arbitrary maintainer scripts (preinst/postinst) with root privileges at install time.
rules.reversible_note: The package can be removed, but install-time maintainer scripts may have already made changes beyond the package's own files.

rules.description: The -P/--purge flag removes a package along with its configuration files, which is not undone by simply reinstalling.
Manages Debian packages at a low level. Read-only subcommands (-l, -s, -L) do not alter system state.
